te: Following up the report on graduates for the labour market, and study themes for fiscal year 2027
se: The meeting considered 3 matters. First, follow-up on the study report on policy recommendations for developing graduates with the knowledge, competencies and ethics the labour market needs; the Cabinet acknowledged the response to the report on 22 September 2025. Related agencies agreed in principle with points such as competency-based curricula, a credit bank system, cooperative and work-integrated education (CWIE), and the Thailand Plus Package tax deduction of 2.5 times. Second, the key themes to study in fiscal year 2027, such as equal access to education, university governance reform, lifelong learning, STEM manpower, and intensive 8-month work placements in the final semester of year 4. Third, a matter on the welfare of university staff that the committee asked the subcommittee to consider, such as preparation for retirement and provident fund contributions. The meeting agreed to first prepare reports on the key themes already set in the fiscal year 2027 work plan.
it: Follow-up on the study report on policy recommendations for developing graduates to meet labour market needs (acknowledged by the Cabinet on 22 September 2025)
Key themes and study visit plan for fiscal year 2027: access to education, university governance, lifelong learning, STEM manpower and CWIE
Welfare and human resource management of university staff (assigned by the committee)

Meeting 39/2569 · Subcommittee on Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation
The national research and innovation information system: setting research questions and cutting duplication
se: The meeting considered the national research and innovation information system and how research databases can be used to set research questions, cut duplication and help universities build specialist strengths. Thailand Science Research and Innovation (TSRI) and the National Research Council of Thailand (NRCT) were invited to give information. TSRI said the Science, Research and Innovation Promotion Fund is split into 3 parts: the Fundamental Fund, 32 per cent, allocated directly to about 200 universities and research agencies; the Strategic Fund, 64 per cent, allocated through programme management units; and the Science and Technology Development Fund, 4 per cent. The current research and innovation plan (2023–2027) has 4 strategies and 15 flagship programmes, and the 4th plan (2028–2032) is open for public comment. NRCT explained the NRIIS system, the central hub for research data from proposal to stored results, and its work to build understanding of the personal data protection law. Suggestions at the meeting included opening general data to the public while restricting sensitive data, pooling funds to develop a Thai large language model (Thai LLM), promoting “One Research One Product”, and having the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation act as lead agency so that all research project data goes into the national central database.
it: The national research and innovation information system, and using research databases to set research questions and cut duplication
Allocation of the research and innovation promotion fund in 3 parts, and the research and innovation plan 2023–2027 (TSRI)
The NRIIS system, research data management, and rights in research results under the Research and Innovation Utilization Promotion Act B.E. 2021 (NRCT)
Suggestions: open general data and restrict sensitive data, develop a Thai LLM, promote One Research One Product, and have a lead agency gather research data into a central database

Higher education cooperation with a university in the United Kingdom
se: The meeting considered ways of international cooperation in higher education, meeting with representatives of a university from the United Kingdom and of the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation. The university presented examples of cooperation, such as transnational education, doctoral study for Thai lecturers and researchers without having to live abroad the whole time, and alumni networks. The meeting discussed cooperation on lifelong learning, such as online courses for working people linked to Thailand's credit bank system in the Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) economy, artificial intelligence, clean energy and health sciences; cooperation with Thai bodies such as the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand and the National Science Museum; and proposals for scholarships for Thai students at bachelor's, master's and doctoral level and for distance learning.
it: Higher education cooperation between Thailand and a university in the United Kingdom (with the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation)
Forms of cooperation: transnational education, doctorates without full-time residence abroad, alumni networks, and online courses linked to the credit bank
Proposals on scholarships for Thai students, and cooperation with the National Astronomical Research Institute of Thailand and the National Science Museum

te: Meeting summary video · Higher education cooperation with a university in the United Kingdom
Reducing inequality in access to higher education, lifelong learning and STEM manpower
se: The meeting considered policy on reducing inequality and creating equal access to higher education, and on developing manpower in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). The Higher Education Quality Enhancement Division and the Manpower Promotion and Development Division of the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation, were invited to give information. They described the National Credit Bank for higher education, which lets learners of all ages build up credits throughout life and transfer learning from training or work experience; the system is expected to be complete in 2028. On equal access, there are scholarships for people in financial need and in remote areas, and grants for students with disabilities; in fiscal year 2026 there were 8,678 scholarship holders, and the central admission (TCAS) application fee is subsidised. On manpower, demand in 2025–2029 is highest in aviation and logistics, and a draft higher education plan for producing and developing the nation's manpower 2028–2032 is being prepared.
it: Equality and lifelong learning in higher education: the National Credit Bank and transfer of learning outcomes
Reducing inequality in access to higher education: scholarships, grants for students with disabilities, and TCAS application fees
STEM manpower development and the draft higher education plan for producing and developing the nation's manpower 2028–2032
